new guideline (Records M1 and S3 show the reference models a task for determining the properties before the parallel start, and the generated model has none. The description's phrasing ('after your customer told you the properties, you can start...') makes the preceding step explicit. Record M6 shows the parallel work is modeled as a task, so the same pattern applies to the preparatory step. The documented guide)

same as LRN-033 (The reference models 'Send the remaining order' and 'Cancel production of the remaining order' as user tasks after the customer's decision. The generated model drops the send step and instead uses a receive task 'Receive customer feedback', which waits for the customer and misrepresents a sending action performed by the process. The reference also uses a userTask for the inspection step, where the)

refines FID-02 (The generated model omits several actions the description states as performed work: determining the properties before production, ordering parts, checking delivery, the inspection step, and sending the remaining order or cancelling it after the customer's decision (M1, M2, M4, M5, M6). It also replaces some of them with a start event for order receipt (X1), a catch event for arrival (X2), and an e)

refines GW-04 (The reference has a user task that captures the customer's required attributes before the parallel ordering fork (M1). The description states that the properties come first and that ordering starts only after they are known (S2, S3). The generated model starts the parallel ordering without this step, so the precondition is missing. No documented or learned guideline asks for a specification-gather)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after an enabling step, several activities of the same kind are to be started in parallel (for example ordering items from various sources), and each activity is named as a separate action: Model each separately described parallel activity as its own task (for example a bpmn:serviceTask when it is an automated call to an external source) placed between the parallel fork and the parallel join that follows the enabling step. Do not omit these activities or merge them into a single task or a bare sequence flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after an enabling step, several activities of the same kind are to be started in parallel (for example ordering items from various sources), and each activity is named as a separate action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that items are ordered from outside sources in parallel and their later arrival is described as a separate event that must happen before a manual step can follow: Model the ordering of the items as its own task on a branch leaving the parallel split, separate from the event that the items arrive. Model the arrival as a distinct intermediate catch event that is waited for before the step that uses the items, and do not merge the ordering and the arrival into one element or omit the ordering task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that items are ordered from outside sources in parallel and their later arrival is described as a separate event that must happen before a manual step can follow

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the organization's work on an order can start only after the customer has communicated the requirements, and that the organization then starts several activities in parallel: Model the organization's own step of establishing or recording the customer's requirements as a separate task performed by the organization, placed before the parallel split that starts the parallel activities. Do not omit this task just because the description mentions only the customer's communication and the parallel activities.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the organization's work on an order can start only after the customer has communicated the requirements, and that the organization then starts several activities in parallel

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant performs an action that is a step of the process, such as communicating an outcome to another party or collecting feedback from a party, and that action happens on only one branch of a decision or after the main work is done: Model each such performed action as a task, placed on every branch where the description states it occurs and in the order the description gives. Do not replace the performed action with an intermediate throw or catch event. Reserve intermediate events for occurrences the process waits for or reacts to.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the process itself performs an action directly toward an outside party (for example handing over a finished item, or a partial delivery) and then continues the sequence based on that party's reaction

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several actions that a participant performs in sequence, and some of them come before a parallel split, after a decision, or on a branch that ends the process: Model each stated action as its own task (userTask, manualTask, or serviceTask according to who performs it), placed in the order the description gives and connected by sequence flows. Do not drop a stated action, and do not stand in for it with a start, catch, or end event. A wait for an external occurrence stays an intermediate catch event, but the stated work that checks or handles that occurrence is still a task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists several actions that a participant performs in sequence, and some of them come before a parallel split, after a decision, or on a branch that ends the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a party supplies the required specifications or attributes of the item to be built, and that obtaining the components or parts starts only after those attributes are known, for example as a parallel fan-out: Model the act of recording those specifications as a human activity placed before the parallel split that starts component procurement, so the split is reached only after the specifications are known. Use a user task when the person captures the specifications in software, and a verb-object label taken from the description's wording. Do not leave this step implicit or move it into the procurement branches.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a party supplies the required specifications or attributes of the item to be built, and that obtaining the components or parts starts only after those attributes are known, for example as a parallel fan-out
